extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners building or evaluating clickbait detectors for news/social headlines
extracted.subtask_description: Binary classification (and related spoiling tasks) to decide whether a news/social headline exhibits clickbait characteristics, optionally using associated article text; includes creation/harmonization of datasets, handcrafted informativeness features, embedding representations, and model evaluation. Also covers abstractive/extractive spoiling as a related subtask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Clickbait is a title that is intentionally sensational, misleading, or emotionally manipulative in order to attract clicks, often by exaggerating, omitting key facts, or creating a curiosity gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the working definition for label assignment and for prompt-based LLM baselines (see LLM prompt rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Task definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a headline (and optionally its associated article), determine whether the headline exhibits clickbait characteristics (binary classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task variants include title-only detection, title+body detection, and spoiling (extractive/abstractive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction & harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine multiple public datasets (Kaggle-1, Kaggle-2, Clickbait Challenge 2017, SemEval Spoiling) with light harmonization: English-only, drop empty titles and duplicates, harmonize fields to title/label across sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CC17, use targetTitle (fallback first postText) and binarize graded annotations via truthMedian ≥ 0.5 (also checked 0.33/0.66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Train/validation/test splits and balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use stratified splits: 80% training, 10% validation, 10% test; option to create a balanced sample (e.g., 20,000/20,000 for title-only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratification used for reproducibility; random seeds fixed (42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtask formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Three working sets: (1) Title-only detection (concatenated datasets); (2) Title+body detection (subset with both title and body); (3) Spoiling (SemEval dataset with abstractive/extractive spoilers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For abstractive spoiling, drop rows with missing humanSpoiler; splits stratified by tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative informativeness measures (compact set)
rubrics_metrics.description: A compact set exemplified in Table 2: Word Count, Common Words Ratio, Capital Letters Ratio, Superlatives Ratio, Flesch Reading-Ease Score (FRES), Polarity, Title–body Cosine Similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These representative measures are part of a larger battery of 25 measures (full definitions in Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full set of 25 informativeness measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete battery of 25 stylistic and linguistic measures (see A.1/Table 5) used to quantify informativeness: character count; word count; mean word length; common words ratio; capital letters ratio; capital words count; punctuation ratio; bait punctuation count; non-bait punctuation count; numbers count; pronouns; 2nd person pronouns; superlatives ratio; speculatives usage; bait phrases usage; title–body similarity (Word2Vec); polarity; subjectivity; TTR; CTTR; Maas index; HD-D (hypergeometric diversity); FRES; FKGL; ARI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures capture readability, lexical diversity, sentiment, pronoun usage, punctuation patterns, numerals, and bait lexemes; full equations and operationalization in Appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of characters (including whitespaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of characters in the title, including whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as one of the 25 informativeness measures (Table 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of words (word count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of words in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of length/informativeness; part of the measures set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean word length
rubrics_metrics.description: Average length of words in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributes to readability estimates and lexical complexity measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common words ratio (percentage of stop words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of stop words to total words in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher common words ratio is folded into EaseOfText and used in baitness calculation (see A.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital letters ratio (percentage of uppercase characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of uppercase characters in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in EyeCatch subcomponent of the composite baitness score; signals shouting/attention-grabbing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital words count (number of fully capitalized words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of fully capitalized words in the title (excluding one-letter words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts of fully capitalized words are considered attention cues and part of the measures set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation ratio (percentage of punctuation/special characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of punctuation and special characters in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation is further subdivided into bait punctuation (e.g. ! " ( ? #) vs non-bait punctuation (e.g. , . ; : - /).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bait punctuation count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of punctuation characters typically associated with bait titles (e.g., ! " ( ? #).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in EyeCatch calculation for baitness; signals attention-seeking punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-bait punctuation count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of punctuation characters associated with non-bait titles (e.g., $ % & , . ; : - /).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to contrast punctuation patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of numbers (not digits) in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerals often appear in listicle-style clickbait; included in EyeCatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronouns (total pronoun count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pronouns in the title (e.g., 'she', 'his', 'you').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronoun usage, especially second-person, informs Curiosity and personalization signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-person pronouns (count of 'you','your', etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of 'you', 'your', 'yours', 'yourself', 'yourselves' in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High 2nd-person pronoun usage signals direct address and attention-grabbing; part of Curiosity subcomponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superlatives ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of adjectives/adverbs in superlative form in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superlatives (e.g., 'best', 'biggest') are strong bait signals and weighted in Curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculatives usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of speculative modal words like 'may', 'might', 'possibly'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative language can create curiosity gaps and is included in Curiosity calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bait phrases usage (count of clickbait lexemes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of known clickbait lexemes (e.g., 'tweets', 'hilarious', and other bait words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit lexeme lists contribute to Curiosity and overall baitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title–body similarity (cosine similarity, Word2Vec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosine similarity between title and article body (Word2Vec-based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low similarity may indicate information gap / mismatch between title and content; included in measures and in final feature set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment polarity (TextBlob)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment polarity score of the title text (TextBlob).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polarity is used in Sentiment subcomponent of baitness: Sentiment = |Polarity| * Subjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity (TextBlob)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjectivity score of the title text (TextBlob).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interacts with polarity in Sentiment subcomponent of baitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type–token ratio (TTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of lexical diversity: t / n (types over tokens) or other normalized variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as part of lexical diversity measures; variants like CTTR and HD-D are also used.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTTR (corrected TTR) / Maas index / hypergeometric diversity (HD-D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative lexical diversity measures: CTTR (TTR adjusted for sample size), Maas index, and HD-D (average TTR on samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture lexical variety and complexity across titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability indices: FRES, FKGL, ARI
rubrics_metrics.description: Readability scores: Flesch Reading-Ease Score (FRES), Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Automated Readability Index (ARI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EaseOfText component uses min(1, FRES/100) and common words ratio; readability contributes to baitness and informativeness modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baitness composite score
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite baitness score defined as the average of four subcomponents: EyeCatch, Curiosity, Sentiment, EaseOfText. Subcomponents are computed from normalized combinations of measures (formulas provided in Appendix A.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EyeCatch = normalized(BaitPunct + 3·CapitalsRatio + Numbers)/3; Curiosity = normalized(2ndPronouns + 2·Superlatives + Speculatives + BaitWords)/4; Sentiment = |Polarity|·Subjectivity; EaseOfText = min(1, FRES/100) + min(1, 1.5·CommonWordsRatio)/2. Composite averaged across subcomponents and clipped to [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature selection: 15 handcrafted informativeness features
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset of 15 explicit, linguistically motivated features (handcrafted informativeness features) used in the best-performing hybrid model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 15 features encode salient cues (second-person pronouns, superlatives, numerals, attention punctuation, readability, similarity, sentiment) and improve interpretability and calibration when combined with embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation methods & settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate multiple textual representations: TF–IDF (ngram_range (1,2), raw vs cleaned), Word2Vec (mean-pooled; Google News 300d and in-house CBOW), GloVe (100d), and transformer/OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-large; dimensions {3072,1000,100,30}; L2 normalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent feature extraction and evaluation setup maintained across representations; dimensionality reduction used for some OpenAI sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model families and baselines to compare
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare tree ensembles (Random Forest, XGBoost), fine-tuned transformer classifiers (RoBERTa), and prompt-based LLM baselines (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-3 Flash) and centroid-based classifiers paired with TF–IDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baselines contextualize performance across lexical, static embedding, transformer embedding, and prompting approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid modeling & fusion strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Early fusion by concatenating the handcrafted 15-measure vector with sentence embeddings (reduced-dimensional OpenAI embeddings) and training XGBoost as the final classifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: XGBoost chosen due to top F1 and calibration; emphasizes complementary signal between explicit stylistic features and dense semantic embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Select models based primarily on F1-score measured on the validation set; report final results on the held-out test set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1 used as primary criterion for model selection; calibration and AUC also reported and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold tuning policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold tuning is considered, but the default classification threshold of 0.5 is used for consistency across experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold adjustments may be explored but were not applied to final reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics and formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, and ROC–AUC. The manuscript provides definitions/formulas for Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1 = 2·(Precision·Recall)/(Precision+Recall); Accuracy = (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN); Precision = TP/(TP+FP); Recall = TP/(TP+FN). AUC computed for ROC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation study protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct formal ablations to compare embeddings-only, features-only, and combined hybrid models to quantify the contribution of handcrafted informativeness features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report F1 differences and ∆ improvements (e.g., hybrid model improved F1 by +4.5 points vs embeddings-only in reported experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt-based LLM classification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM prompt constraints for zero-shot and few-shot classification: base decision only on the title; do not provide explanations; output only a single digit (0 non-clickbait, 1 clickbait); follow the provided clickbait definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for strict classifier baselines; few-shot prompts include labeled examples for clickbait and non-clickbait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt shot settings and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Test zero-shot, few-shot, and one-shot prompt configurations with constrained outputs; exact prompt templates and exemplar selection detailed in Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt engineering and exemplar selection affect few-shot LLM baseline performance; output constraints enforced to get labels only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental environment & reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental environment: local CPU-only workstation (32 GB RAM), Python 3.11, scikit-learn, XGBoost, spaCy, Hugging Face Transformers, OpenAI API for embeddings; random seeds fixed to 42 and stratified splits for reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All data preparation, feature extraction, and model training conducted with specified stack; final models and code released to support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance reporting and interpretability objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Report comparative performance across models and emphasize interpretability: explicit features highlight salient linguistic cues (second-person pronouns, superlatives, numerals, attention punctuation) to enable transparent and well-calibrated predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretability is a stated goal; handcrafted features chosen to provide human-understandable signals complementary to embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibration of classifier outputs is considered when selecting the final model (XGBoost chosen for top F1 and calibration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration matters for user-facing warnings and probabilistic outputs; default decision threshold remains 0.5 for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of embedding dimensionality experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate multiple OpenAI embedding sizes (3072d, 1000d, 100d, 30d) and report relative performance; reduced-dimensional embeddings may be combined with features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different embedding sizes affect performance and complementarity with handcrafted features; dimensionality reduction and L2 normalization applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline performance benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comprehensive baselines spanning traditional lexical TF–IDF + centroid classifiers, Word2Vec/GloVe embedding pipelines, fine-tuned transformers, and prompt-based LLMs to contextualize hybrid model gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC across baselines and proposed models.
